bib.title: GUI-R1: A Generalist R1-Style Vision-Language Action Model For GUI Agents

read.skipped: Figures 1, 3, 4, 5 extract as axis labels only; no values read from them. No appendix exists.

question: Can rule-based reinforcement fine-tuning (GRPO) with a unified action-space reward, on a small curated dataset, make a vision-language model a better GUI agent for high-level tasks than SFT on large data?
hypothesis: RFT with verifiable rewards generalises better and is more data-efficient than SFT for GUI action prediction, including unseen interfaces.
contributions: GUI-R1, the first framework using rule-based reinforcement fine-tuning to enhance reasoning of LVLMs in high-level GUI action prediction.
A rule-based unified action space reward function that validates responses across platforms and task granularities.
GUI-R1-3K, a high-quality fine-tuning dataset built with that reward function.
Evaluation on eight benchmarks over three platforms and three task granularities.

method.summary: Qwen2.5-VL 3B/7B is fine-tuned with GRPO (EasyR1) on GUI-R1-3K, a 3K-example set filtered by the base model's own rollout accuracy. The policy emits <think> reasoning and an <answer> action; reward is a weighted sum of a format reward and an accuracy reward (action type, click-in-bbox, text F1>0.5) over a unified action space.
method.task: GUI action prediction from screenshot, high-level instruction and action history (grounding, low-level and high-level tasks)

datasets.name: Raw GUI pool (FineWeb, UIBert, AMEX, RICOSCA, parts of SeeClick and OS-Atlas pretraining data)
datasets.size: ~14M examples of grounding and low-level data, plus ~30K high-level examples from OS-Atlas instruction data
datasets.preprocessing: Qwen2.5VL-7B generates 10 responses per example; examples with estimated accuracy 0 or 1 removed, leaving 140K low-level and 1.5K high-level

datasets.name: GUI-R1-3K
datasets.size: 3K examples (1.5K high-level plus 1.5K randomly sampled low-level)
datasets.source: built by the authors from the pool above

datasets.name: ScreenSpot-Pro
datasets.size: 23 applications, five industries, three operating systems

other.use: 10 rollouts per example to estimate difficulty

models.name: OS-Atlas-4B/7B, UI-R1-3B, SeeClick, ShowUI-2B, CogAgent-18B, Aria-GUI, UGround-7B, Claude, GPT-4o, QwenVL-7B

training.objective: GRPO: A_i = (r_i - mean({r})) / std({r}) over N sampled responses, updated under KL constraint; response reward R_o = alpha*R_f + beta*R_acc, R_acc = R_act + R_point + R_text
training.epochs: RFT: nine epochs (EasyR1); SFT baseline: one epoch (LLaMA Factory)

other.alpha_beta_default: inferred: alpha 0.2, beta 0.8 (best row of Table 4, which equals the reported GUI-R1-3B row of Table 3)
other.image_resolution: 1,048,576 pixels default; 2,097,152 pixels in the doubled-resolution ablation (read from the text of 4.3)
other.training_curves_x_axis: Figure 5 x-axis runs to about 90 steps (read from Fig 5 axis labels)

inference.samples: single zero-shot pass per item; no repeats or seeds stated
inference.prompting: One unified, simple zero-shot prompt for all compared methods; the action-space prompt lists actions [complete, close/delete, press home, click, press back, type, select, scroll, enter]; grounding prompt allows only [click]

metrics.name: Type
metrics.definition: exact match between predicted and ground-truth action type

metrics.name: GR (Grounding)
metrics.definition: accuracy of predicted click point (inside ground-truth bbox)

metrics.name: SR
metrics.definition: step success rate: step correct only if predicted action and its arguments (point for click, input text) are correct

eval.protocol: Test splits only; metrics follow OS-Atlas; single run, no significance tests or seeds reported.

prompts.text: You are GUI-R1, a reasoning GUI Agent Assistant. In this UI screenshot < image >, I want you to continue executing the command task, with the action history being history. Please provide the action to perform (enumerate from [complete, close/delete, press home, click, press back, type, select, scroll, enter]), the point where the cursor is moved to (integer) if a click is performed, and any input text required to complete the action. Output the thinking process in <think> </think> tags, and the final answer in <answer> </answer> tags as follows: <think> ... </think> <answer>[‘action’: enum[complete, close/delete, press home, click, press back, type, select, scroll, enter], ‘point’: [x, y], ‘input text’: ‘no input text [default]’]</answer>.
Same as the task prompt but the action enumeration is [click] only.

evidence.quote: For RFT, we use the EasyR1 [26] framework for training over nine epochs.
All experiments are conducted using 8×NVIDIA A100-80G GPUs.

results.claim: GUI-R1-3B beats the SFT-on-same-data 3B model on ScreenSpot.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-VL-3B; RFT on GUI-R1-3K vs SFT on same 3K; zero-shot prompt; ScreenSpot test
results.note: These aggregate numbers are not printed in Table 1, which lists per-category text/icon cells only.

results.claim: GUI-R1-3B beats the SFT-on-same-data 3B model on ScreenSpot-Pro.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-VL-3B; RFT vs SFT on GUI-R1-3K; ScreenSpot-Pro test
results.note: Not printed in Table 1; the text reports it as an 82.8% relative improvement.

results.claim: Average low-level success rate rises from the zero-shot 3B base to GUI-R1-3B.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-VL-3B zero-shot vs GUI-R1-3B; GUI-Act-Web, OmniAct-Web, OmniAct-Desktop, AndroidControl-Low
results.quote: with the average success rate increasing from 55.65 to 80.88 at the 3B scale

results.claim: GUI-R1-7B has the highest overall low-level score in Table 2.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-VL-7B; baseline is zero-shot QwenVL2.5-7B (SFT-on-3K 7B scores 80.09, OS-Atlas-7B 70.07)
results.table: Table 2, row GUI-R1-7B, column Overall (83.30); row QwenVL2.5-7B (79.05)

results.claim: GUI-R1-3B improves overall high-level score over GPT-4o by an absolute 21.06.
results.setup: AndroidControl-High and GUI-Odyssey; GPT-4o overall 28.69, GUI-R1-3B overall 49.75
results.quote: our 3B-scale method achieves an absolute improvement of 21.06

results.claim: GUI-R1-7B reaches 56.13 overall on high-level tasks, above zero-shot Qwen2.5-VL-7B and SFT-3K 7B.
results.setup: AndroidControl-High and GUI-Odyssey; baseline zero-shot QwenVL2.5-7B; SFT 7B* scores 50.97
results.table: Table 3, row GUI-R1-7B, column Overall (56.13); row QwenVL2.5-7B (50.53)

results.claim: GUI-R1-3B improves on UI-R1-3B (RFT on low-level grounding) by 3.4 points on average on high-level tasks.
results.setup: 3B scale, AndroidControl-High and GUI-Odyssey; GUI-R1-3B 49.75 vs UI-R1-3B 46.35
results.quote: our model achieves an average improvement of 3.4 points at the 3B scale

results.claim: GUI-R1-3B has a 27.2% lead over UI-R1 in step success rate on GUI-Odyssey.
results.quote: 27.2% lead in the step success rate on GUI-Odyssey
results.note: Text calls it 27.2%; (41.33-32.49)/32.49 is about 27.2% relative. Written as 'points' elsewhere would be wrong.

results.claim: Low-level scores for GUI-R1-3B exceed UI-R1 by about 10 points.
results.quote: our model achieves a 10-point improvement at the 3B scale

results.claim: Data efficiency: GUI-R1 uses 3K examples versus the OS-Atlas corpus.
results.quote: using only 0.02% of the data (3K vs. 13M)
results.note: Inconsistent: Section 4.2 says 0.2% (3K vs. 14M) and Section 3.3 says ~14M collected examples. 3K/13M is about 0.023%; 3K/14M about 0.021%, so 0.02% is arithmetically right and 0.2% is not.

results.claim: Lower format-reward weight improves high-level performance monotonically.
results.setup: alpha/beta = 0.2/0.8 vs 0.8/0.2 (0.5/0.5 gives 47.72); AndroidControl-High and GUI-Odyssey; 3B inferred
results.table: Table 4, rows alpha 0.2 beta 0.8 (49.75) and alpha 0.8 beta 0.2 (46.48), column Overall
results.note: The 0.8/0.2 row repeats the UI-R1-3B numbers of Table 3 (57.85, 55.70, 45.44, 52.16, 34.46, 32.49) but its overall is 46.48 versus 46.35 in Table 3.

results.claim: Filtered data converges faster and to a higher reward than unfiltered; doubled image resolution speeds convergence and lifts the ceiling.
results.setup: Fig 4, reward vs training steps; resolution 1,048,576 to 2,097,152 pixels; only qualitative in text

results.claim: No 'aha moment' appears: mean response length first falls then slowly rises.
results.setup: Fig 5d; the authors attribute it to single-image, non-interactive training

limits: Evaluation is offline, step-wise on static screenshots (Type/GR/SR); no live interactive environment or end-to-end task completion.
Authors concede the 'aha moment' did not occur, perhaps because training is single-image and non-interactive; multi-image interactive training is future work.
Optimizer, learning rate, batch size, rollouts per prompt, KL coefficient, steps and seeds are not stated; no variance or significance reported.
SFT baseline is trained on only the 3K set, one epoch, so it is not a tuned SFT comparison; RFT gets nine epochs.
Data-efficiency comparison with OS-Atlas mixes a 3K RFT set on a strong Qwen2.5-VL base against 13-14M examples SFT; fraction is printed as 0.02% and 0.2% in different places.
Data filtering uses Qwen2.5VL-7B itself, so the training set is tailored to that base.
Future work: multi-agent collaboration and error-correction policies.

terms.definition: extracts action space categories across different platforms and integrates them into a unified action space, so all high-level instructions decompose into atomic actions
action type exact-match; GUI grounding accuracy of click point; step success rate requiring correct action and arguments

lineage.note: previous SOTA SFT; also source of data and metrics

figures.caption: GUI-R1 achieves the best performance on eight evaluation datasets covering various platforms and task granularities, demonstrating the promising potential of RFT in GUI agent tasks.
figures.why: Radar charts compare all models across grounding, low-level and high-level benchmarks at once.

figures.caption: Overview of the GUI-R1 Framework. Given the high-level instruction, action history, and visual image inputs, the policy model generates multiple responses containing reasoning steps. Then the verifiable rewards, such as action type reward, click point reward, and input text reward, are used with the policy gradient optimization algorithm to update the policy model.
figures.why: Shows the rollout-reward-GRPO loop with a worked think/answer output.

figures.caption: Ablation study of image resolution and data quality.
figures.why: Reward vs steps for three data/resolution settings.

figures.caption: Visualization of the training process of GUI-R1: format reward, accuracy reward, mean response length, and PG loss vs steps.
figures.why: Shows format reward saturating early and response length not growing.

code.snippet: R_o = alpha*R_f + beta*R_acc ; R_acc = R_act + R_point + R_text ; R_point = 1 if o_point in gt_bbox else 0 ; R_text = 1 if F1(o_text, gt_text) > 0.5 else 0

problems: Figures 1, 3, 4, 5 and tables extract as one value per line; table rows were read by position and the headline numbers cross-checked against the text.
Inconsistent data-fraction claim: 0.02% (3K vs 13M) in abstract/intro vs 0.2% (3K vs 14M) in 4.2.
Table 4 row alpha 0.8/beta 0.2 repeats UI-R1-3B per-metric numbers from Table 3 but overall differs (46.48 vs 46.35).
Section 4.2 cites GUI-Act-Web as [29] (ScreenSpot-Pro) while the reference list has it as [30].
